title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities crosses spatial and taxonomic boundaries without detectable homogenization
frozen_core_claims: Recent-rain conditions are associated with expansion of the behaviourally realized acoustic community across both spatial footprint and taxonomic richness.
Local alpha richness and route gamma richness increase with rainfall contrast, while measured among-active-site beta-diversity metrics show no detectable shift.
Active species x active-site matrix fill is practically equivalent within the prespecified +/-0.05 connectance-slope margin in primary and exact-consecutive-year samples.

Most rainfall-associated species x stop incidence growth crosses at least one spatial and/or taxonomic matrix boundary; within-core rearrangement accounts for only about 8 percent of the total incidence slope.
The main multiscale expansion signal persists after adjustment for recorded hearing impairment, timeouts and wind, with traffic and MassNoiseIndex sensitivities agreeing.
frozen_interpretation: Expansion without detectable homogenization: the observed active community becomes larger across sites and species, but measured among-site compositional differentiation does not detectably collapse.
frozen_negative_boundaries: Activation geometry is not a rainfall-specific response trait and remains Supporting Information only after placebo failure.
No week-long pulse or compositional reassembly claim.
No rainfall causality, occupancy change, colonization, extinction or demographic metacommunity claim.
No claim that all beta-diversity quantities are equivalent or exactly invariant.
No new species-trait mechanism may replace the failed activation-geometry candidate within RC6.
